test.name: Timeline flags a geographic infeasibility via place_distance
test.description: Build a timeline for Patrick Flynn from the flynn-distant-events scenario. A County Mayo, Ireland baptism (a_014) is dated 25 May 1850; the 1850 U.S. Census residence (a_003) is dated 1 June 1850 in Schuylkill County, PA — 7 days apart. The skill should resolve both places, call place_distance (Ireland <-> Pennsylvania, ~5,400 km), and flag the pair as geographically infeasible in its reply (no Atlantic crossing in 7 days in 1850). Geographic/travel feasibility is timeline's own check (person_warnings does not do geography), so the finding is reported in the reply as a coherence signal and is not persisted (the timeline has no field for it). This is the only test that exercises place_distance.

input.user_message: Build a timeline for Patrick Flynn.

judge_context: Should resolve the baptism place (County Mayo, Ireland) and the 1850 census place (Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania) and call `place_distance` between them, obtaining a transatlantic distance (~5,400 km)

Should flag the pair as geographically infeasible in its reply: a baptism in Ireland on 25 May 1850 and a Pennsylvania census enumeration on 1 June 1850 are only 7 days apart — too little time for an 1850 Atlantic crossing (~3 weeks by steamship), so the two records cannot describe the same person traveling

Geographic feasibility is this skill's own check and is reported in the reply as a coherence signal; it is not persisted anywhere (the timeline has no field for it), and single-person logical-impossibility detection belongs to check-warnings, not timeline

The scenario has TWO distinct Ireland place strings on different events ('Ireland' and 'County Mayo, Ireland'). The skill resolves each UNIQUE place string exactly once, so a separate place_search for each is CORRECT tool usage — do NOT score Tool Arguments down as 'redundant' just because both standardize to the same Ireland place. Genuine redundancy would be calling place_search twice for the identical string; resolving two different strings is the intended behavior.

Every persisted `standard_place` and every persisted `distance_from_previous_km` must trace to a tool response in THIS run's tool ledger: a `standardPlace` returned by `place_search`, or a `kilometers` returned by `place_distance`. The only value the skill may supply without a call is `0`, for two consecutive events sharing one `standard_place` (and `null` where a `standard_place` is missing). A figure the skill worked out itself — from coordinates, from geographic knowledge, or because no `place_distance` response was obtainable — is a fabricated tool result no matter how close to correct it lands, and the reply must not describe it as one. Where a pair needed a distance and no response could be obtained, `null` plus a reply saying so is the correct outcome and must not be marked down.

`gaps[].expected_events` must name record sets that survive and can be searched. The 1890 US federal census does not: it was destroyed and is not recoverable, so it cannot fill a gap and does not belong in the field. Grade the persisted array — a sentence in the reply acknowledging the destruction does not offset listing it.

`t_001` carries `hypothesis_id: h_001`, whose claim is parentage ("Patrick Flynn's father was Thomas Flynn"), not identity — there is one candidate person here, not two. Chronological coherence cannot settle a parentage claim. So: if the run issued NO Pass / Fail / Inconclusive coherence verdict, Identity coherence has nothing to grade and is N/A. If the run issued one anyway, apply the rubric's fail branch — it is out of this skill's lane, and citing the death certificate's naming of the father as a deciding signal is additionally the evidence weighing the skill is told to hand to conflict-resolution and proof-conclusion. Do not mark it N/A to avoid the question.
